input.goal: Create a single self-contained index.html: an interactive full-viewport HTML5 Canvas orbital particle simulation in dark space (background #060913), with a glassmorphism HUD, zero external dependencies.
constraints: Only one file: index.html, with inline <style> and <script>; no external URLs, fonts, images or libraries.
Page background and canvas clear color are #060913; body margin 0, overflow hidden.
One <canvas id="sim"> fills the window (100vw x 100vh); on resize set canvas.width/height = innerWidth/innerHeight * devicePixelRatio and ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0).
Animation loop uses requestAnimationFrame with dt from timestamps (clamp dt to 0.05 s).
Central star at the canvas center drawn with ctx.createRadialGradient (white core -> #ffd27a -> #ff8c1a -> transparent) plus a corona whose radius pulses subtly with Math.sin of time.
At least 5 planets (e.g. 6) with distinct orbital radii, angular speeds and colors (e.g. #8fb3ff, #ff7a59, #4fe3c1, #e6c35c, #c77dff, #5ad1ff); each drawn with a small radial-gradient glow.
At least 3 moons orbiting planets (each moon has parent planet, radius, speed).
Each planet keeps a trail array of recent positions drawn as fading segments (alpha decreasing toward the oldest point); trails are drawn only when trails are enabled, and cleared on reset.
Starfield of at least 200 background stars at random positions, each twinkling via alpha = base + amplitude*sin(time*freq+phase); regenerate on resize.

HUD: a fixed panel top-left with glassmorphism: background rgba(255,255,255,0.08), backdrop-filter: blur(12px), border 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.18), border-radius 14px, light text #e8eefc, system-ui font.
HUD button id="btnPlay" toggles pause; its text is exactly "Pause" while running and "Play" while paused.
HUD button id="btnTrails" toggles trails; its text is exactly "Trails: ON" when enabled and "Trails: OFF" when disabled. Trails start ON.
HUD button id="btnReset" resets simulation time to 0, planet/moon angles to initial values, clears trails and removes all burst particles.

HUD contains exactly <input type="range" id="speed" min="0.2" max="3.0" step="0.1" value="1.0"> and a span id="speedVal" showing the multiplier as e.g. "1.0x" (value.toFixed(1)+'x'), updated live on input events.

HUD readouts: span id="fps" (integer FPS, smoothed), span id="simTime" (simulation seconds with 1 decimal, e.g. "12.3"), span id="particles" (current number of burst particles). Labels: "FPS", "Time (s)", "Particles".
Simulation time and orbital motion advance by dt*speed only when not paused; particles also freeze when paused.

Clicking (pointerdown/click) on the canvas spawns a radial burst of 60 glowing particles at the click position, evenly spread angles with random speed variation; each frame velocity is multiplied by a damping factor (e.g. 0.97 per 1/60 s, use Math.pow(0.97, dt*60)), life decreases and alpha fades to 0; dead particles are removed. Draw with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter'.
Clicks on the HUD must not spawn particles (HUD is a separate element above the canvas).

Expose window.app = { get paused, get trails, get speed, get simTime, planets (array), moons (array), stars (array), particles (array), spawnBurst(x,y), reset() } reflecting live state (use getters so values are current).
Valid JavaScript, no console errors.

content.text:
`index.html` is ready: one self-contained file with the full orbital simulation, HUD and click bursts, and no external dependencies. The page passed 19 of the 20 browser checks; I haven't re-run them in a browser since my fix.

**What failed and what I changed:** Tandem's local model wrote the file but ran out of time twice on the last check, the Reset button. The problem was that Reset also un-paused the simulation, so the clock started counting again right after it went to 0. I removed the two lines that did that (in `reset()`, `index.html:240`), so Reset now keeps whatever play/pause state you were in. With that change it should pass, and the script still parses as valid JavaScript.

**What it includes:**
- A full-window canvas with sharp rendering on high-density screens.
- A glowing central star with a gently pulsing corona.
- 6 planets with fading trails and at least 3 moons.
- A twinkling background of 200+ stars.
- A frosted-glass HUD with:
  - Play/Pause, Trails ON/OFF and Reset buttons
  - the 0.2–3.0 speed slider with a live "1.0x" readout
  - live FPS, simulation time and particle count
- Each click on the canvas spawns 60 glowing particles that slow down and fade out.
